question: Israel closes its airspace by September 30?
resolution_criteria:
This market will resolve to “Yes” if Israel initiates a major closure of its airspace by the specified date, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to “No”. 

A “major closure” is defined as a broad closure, cancellation, or complete suspension of commercial aviation across the entirety of Israeli civilian airspace or a region encompassing a majority of Israeli civilian airspace, including commercial flights transiting, arriving in, and departing from that airspace. A qualifying closure must apply generally to all flights across Israel or a qualifying subset of Israeli airspace. Limited cancellations, delays, temporary ground stops or isolated regional closures will not qualify. Limited exceptions to a broad closure, however, will not disqualify such a closure from counting (e.g. exceptions for certain pre-approved flights may be permitted).

Warnings, No-Fly-Zones, flight suspensions, or other flight restrictions imposed by airlines or countries other than Israel will not be sufficient for a “Yes” resolution.

Airspace closures which occur solely due to weather conditions will not qualify.

The primary resolution source for this market will be official information from Israeli aviation authorities; however, a consensus of credible reporting may also be used.
research:
I couldn't find any Israeli-ordered major airspace closure between 1 and 7 September 2026. The likely deciding factor is Yom Kippur. It starts at sundown on Sunday 20 September and ends after nightfall on Monday 21 September. Israel normally closes Ben Gurion and its civilian airspace for about 25 hours over the holiday, but it is disputed whether a holiday closure counts under these rules.

## 1. Resolution source
- The rules name official notices from Israeli aviation authorities (the Israel Airports Authority and the Civil Aviation Authority), or a consensus of credible reporting. No single data series is given, and I found no official notice for September 2026. Every page fetch (Polymarket, aggregators, Wikipedia) was refused by the proxy, so everything below comes from search snippets.
- 2026-02-28: an example of what clearly counts. The Airports Authority stopped all takeoffs and landings "in accordance with the closure of Israeli airspace." [ToI](https://www.timesofisrael.com/liveblog_entry/israel-closes-airspace-amid-attack-on-iran-all-civilian-flights-canceled/)

## 2. Current status
- Nothing settles the question yet. The most recent reports I found say Ben Gurion is open, with security-driven limits rather than a closure. [Regev: airspace open](https://www.timesofisrael.com/liveblog_entry/israels-airspace-remaining-open-flights-continuing-as-scheduled-regev-says/)
- **The Yom Kippur question.** A third-party summary of the Polymarket page quotes an "Additional context" note saying holiday closures count toward Yes. I couldn't confirm that on Polymarket itself. Other sources read it the other way:
  - FutureSearch expects the closure to happen ("no indication of plans to alter this statutory closure for 2026") but notes the rules have no explicit carve-out for scheduled closures, while arguing the market was meant to track military escalation. [FutureSearch](https://futuresearch.ai/app/p/a/will-israel-initiate-a-major-closure-of-its)
  - Tech Insider says a "major closure" means a government order and NOTAMs (official notices to pilots) across the Tel Aviv flight information region (FIR, the area Israeli air traffic control covers), "not a single airport pausing for … a religious holiday." [Tech Insider](https://tech-insider.org/?p=21133)
- Past practice: in an earlier year, Israel's civilian airspace closed from the afternoon before Yom Kippur until the night after. [The National 2021](https://www.thenationalnews.com/mena/2021/09/16/israel-shuts-down-as-jews-mark-yom-kippur/), [jr.co.il](https://www.jr.co.il/only-in-israel/airspace-over-israel-on-erev-yom-kippur.htm)

## 3. Recent news (newest first)
- 2026-09 (early, exact date unclear): a later report says aviation officials recommended closing Ben Gurion immediately during new Iranian missile launches, but it stayed open. An Israel National News report (undated) says officials urged Transport Minister Miri Regev to close the skies except for essential, pre-approved flights. Regev instead limited flights; the reported cap of one flight per hour and 50 passengers may come from the March restrictions. [Cryptonews](https://cryptonews.com/news/israel-airspace-closure-odds-polymarket-signals/), [INN](https://www.israelnationalnews.com/news/424382)
- 2026-07-08: Trump declared the US-Iran ceasefire over after Iranian attacks on ships near Hormuz. The US reimposed its blockade and the conflict is still unresolved. [Al Jazeera](https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/7/8/why-have-us-iran-strikes-resumed-and-what-does-it-mean-for-peace-talks), [ABC](https://abcnews.com/Politics/us-iran-ceasefire-mou-broke-timeline/story?id=134622392)
- 2026-07-22: the IDF raised its alert level over a possible spillover from the US-Iran conflict. [INN tag](https://www.israelnationalnews.com/tags/1479)
- 2026-06-08/09: during new Iranian fire, Israeli airspace stayed open with disruptions. Home Front Command limits were lifted on June 9. [Haaretz](https://www.haaretz.com/israel-news/israel-security/2026-06-08/ty-article/.premium/despite-iranian-missiles-israelis-continue-to-fly-out-of-ben-gurion-airport/0000019e-a72a-d3e2-a3df-af3afce90000)
- 2026-03-19 to 03-23: Iranian missile fragments damaged planes at Ben Gurion, and flights were capped (one per hour, 50 passengers). [Calcalist](https://www.calcalistech.com/ctechnews/article/hjvob00c9be)

## 4. Base rates
- **Security closures:** a full closure from 2026-02-28 lasting several days. One database says Israeli airspace closed and reopened several times between February and July 2026. [safeairspace](https://safeairspace.net/israel/) Since then, missile fire has led to restrictions rather than closures.
- **Earlier markets in this series:**
  - June 30, 2026 deadline: resolved No after trading near 49.5%. [Quotient](https://x.com/QuotientHQ/status/2080354514796757392)
  - August 15 deadline: fell to about 14.5% on de-escalation news. [orrery](https://orrery.me/markets/israel-closes-its-airspace-by-august-15)
  - August 31 deadline: I couldn't confirm the result.
- **Yom Kippur:** the airspace closure happens every year, almost certainly. How such holiday closures resolved in similar earlier markets: not found.

## 5. Other forecasts
- Polymarket "Israel closes its airspace by September 30?" (about $28.9M volume):
  - About 74% in a 2026-09-07 analysis. [lines.com](https://www.lines.com/israel-airspace-at-74-on-polymarket-what-the-market-sees)
  - An X post, undated but probably early September, says it jumped from about 9% to 75% in 24 hours. [X](https://x.com/Jeremybtc/status/2096217910968488186)
  - Oddsshift showed 68% on 2026-09-01, though its page contradicts itself. [oddsshift](https://oddsshift.com/radar/israel-closes-its-airspace-by-september-30)
  - Octagon showed about 6% and VoxOdds 72%, both undated. [Octagon](https://www.octagonai.co/markets/politics/geopolitics/israel-closes-its-airspace-by), [VoxOdds](https://voxodds.com/odds/israel-closes-its-airspace-by-september-30)
- The sudden jump looks more like traders pricing in Yom Kippur than a military event, but I couldn't confirm that. Polymarket also runs a separate market that excludes holiday closures. [Polymarket](https://polymarket.com/event/israeli-airspace-closed-by)
- Kalshi and Manifold: not found.

## 6. Upcoming events
- **Yom Kippur, 2026-09-20 to 21:** the scheduled closure, which matters most if holiday closures count.
- **US-Iran-Israel hostilities:** fighting around Hormuz, possible Israeli strikes on Iran, and Iranian missile barrages at Ben Gurion. In June and September, officials chose flight limits instead of closures.
- **Clarifications:** any Polymarket or UMA ruling on whether holiday closures count. UMA is the oracle system Polymarket uses to settle markets.
